checks_run.procedure: D-182's unexplained failure of p5-launch-health-kpi.spec.ts:159 (chromium-ar, locale unset; 'submitted' not visible within 5 s). Reproduction attempts: the full product suite in both locale settings, the test alone in chromium-ar x10 beside a full product run, R7-HEALTH-RACE (the test's ending replayed and instrumented, browser CPU slowed 1x and 4x), and R7-HEALTH-SLOWGET (the test's own waits, every assessment GET delayed 0 or 1500 ms). Plus a code reading of HealthCheckPage/useRunner.
checks_run.command: chain-product.sh (QA-R7-05); run-e2e.sh unset prod 26680 26681 d182repro apps/web/e2e/p5-launch-health-kpi.spec.ts --grep 'Health check: Incomplete' --project=chromium-ar --repeat-each=10; chain-r7-probes3.sh (QA_CPU_RATE=1|4, QA_SLOW_MS=0|1500)
checks_run.environment: Clone at 1932faa, production-initialized stack, Chromium; load up to 10 during the full runs, about 4.5 during the targeted run
checks_run.expected: Establish whether the failure reproduces, and whether it is a product or a test defect.
checks_run.actual: Not reproduced. The test passed in both projects in all 4 full product runs, 10/10 alone in chromium-ar, R7-HEALTH-RACE 5/5 at CPU rate 1 and 5/5 at rate 4, and R7-HEALTH-SLOWGET 6/6 at 0 ms and 6/6 at 1500 ms. In every run the screen sent If-Match equal to the saved version (27), the server answered 200, and 'submitted' appeared in 166-559 ms. Finding: with slow GETs (1500 ms), the test's 'reloaded' wait resolved in 6/6 runs on the GET issued BEFORE the Save-actions click: the refresh after the refused first Submit, version 26. useRunner shows the alert before awaiting that refresh, so the test can proceed while that GET is in flight. The test can therefore click Submit without the saved version on screen. In my runs the click still landed after the post-save GET (about 2000 ms vs 1880 ms), so the product sent the right version. If the order were reversed, the server's 409 (correct optimistic concurrency) would fail the test. Judgement: a test synchronization defect, demonstrated, raised as F-DG5-151 (Low). It is a plausible but unproven cause of the D-182 failure, whose trace is lost. I found no evidence of a product defect. D-182's disclosure (not counted as passed, cause not established) was accurate.
